 Chichibu Night Festival 2026: Dates, Route and Tickets 
 Culture Chichibu Night Festival 2026: Dates, Route and Tickets 
 Confirmed dates 2 and 3 December 2026, the trip from Tokyo, special trains and fares checked. The 2026 timetables are not yet published.
 Updated November 2, 2026 
 14 min read 
 Contents
 Loading…

 Learn more Partners: Viator The Chichibu Night Festival 2026 runs on Wednesday 2 and Thursday 3 December 2026 in Chichibu, about 77 minutes from Ikebukuro by Laview. The 2nd is the eve, the 3rd the main day, with six floats. The city has not yet published the 2026 timetables for the processions or the fireworks.
 Checked on 2 November 2026 against the official sources cited (City of Chichibu, Seibu Railway, Agency for Cultural Affairs). 
 Every early December, the small town of Chichibu, in Saitama Prefecture, hosts one of Japan’s major float festivals. The Chichibu Night Festival (Chichibu Yomatsuri, 秩父夜祭) runs after dark around Chichibu Shrine, with floats pulled by neighbourhood crews and music that goes with every procession. This article draws on the announcements published in October 2026.
 1. The Chichibu Night Festival at a glance
 Photo by Ryo Tanaka on Unsplash A night festival carried by its floats
 Processions free, according to guides 
 2 days: 2 and 3 December 2026 
 Around 4 °C on average 
 Early December, every year The Japanese name, 秩父夜祭, means « Chichibu night festival ». The festival is really about its floats, the yatai, and the music that goes with them. It takes place around Chichibu Shrine, in the town of the same name, at the foot of the Chichibu mountains. The city’s official festival page lists six floats.
 The festival lasts two days. Wednesday 2 December 2026 is the eve, called yoimiya (宵宮). Thursday 3 December 2026 is the main festival, taisai (大祭): the day of the big processions and the fireworks, whose 2026 times have not been published yet. Both dates appear in the city of Chichibu notice , updated on 13 October 2026, and Seibu Railway confirms them in its statement of 28 October 2026.
 English Wikipedia says the festival has been held for more than 300 years. No official source we checked confirms that age.
 On 2 December, the eve, guides describe a lively evening that is calmer than the 3rd.
 Pixidia tip: the special trains on 3 December are capped at 8 tickets per person, and sales open on 3 November 2026. If you plan to go that day, note this date before anything else. 
 Hidden Japan Near Tokyo Temple Walk and Local Life in Chichibu ★ 4.95 · 20  reviews Partner link 
3-hour private visit, €46.82 per person (based on 2 adults), dates for 2 and 3 December 2026 available, checked 2 November 2026
 €46.82 per person 3-hour private visit, (based on 2 adults), dates for 2 and 3 December 2026 available, checked 2 November 2026 
 See dates 2. Six floats, neighbourhood crews and continuous music
 Photo by ayumi kubo on Unsplash Kasaboko and yatai: two kinds of float
 The City of Chichibu describes six floats: two kasaboko (笠鉾), floats with a conical roof topped by an ornament, and four yatai (屋台), multi-storey floats. Guides sometimes call them mobile « stages ». Each float is looked after by the residents of one of the town’s districts (町), who take part in every procession.
 Depending on the float, they weigh between 10 and 20 tonnes, according to the national guide on japan.travel .
 The hayashi music
 Hayashi, a traditional ensemble of flutes and percussion, accompanies the floats.
 Six floats: two kasaboko and four yatai 
 One neighbourhood crew per float 
 Hayashi music during the processions 
 2025 reference: the floats climb the Danzaka slope on the evening of 3 December (the city has not yet detailed the 2026 programme) 
 Pixidia tip: the 2026 procession schedule is not out yet. Follow the city’s notice, which should give the times and traffic restrictions, and allow extra time to walk between viewing points. 3. Recognised in 1979 and 2016
 A national designation, then an international listing
 On 3 February 1979, the Agency for Cultural Affairs designated the Chichibu yatai festival and the kagura as Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties. In 2016, UNESCO added the festivals of floats, hoko and yatai to its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. According to the Agency’s record, these are two separate steps, and the record gives only the year 2016. Guides that cite « December 2016 » go further than the source.
 Two vocabulary traps. The Agency’s file also mentions kagura performances linked to the festival, which do not take place on the festival dates. And the Matsuri Kaikan museum, whose site is chichibu-matsuri.jp , is a museum: it is not the official festival website.
 4. The 2026 calendar: what is confirmed
 Photo by Tokyo Kohaku on Unsplash What the city has published for 2026
 The City of Chichibu notice, updated on 13 October 2026, confirms both evenings: Wednesday 2 December for the eve and Thursday 3 December for the main festival. Seibu Railway confirms both dates in its statement of 28 October 2026.
 The same notice announces details still to come: procession times, the float programme, the fireworks, and traffic and parking restrictions. On 2 November 2026, the date we checked, no newer version had been published.
 The table below therefore uses the 2025 timings. They show roughly what to expect, not a programme. Use them to set your expectations, then check the city notice once it is complete.
 Chichibu Night Festival calendar: confirmed 2026 dates and 2025 reference times Element 2026 (official) 2025 (reference, indicative) 
 Eve (宵宮) Wednesday 2 December Tuesday 2 December 
 Main festival (大祭) Thursday 3 December Wednesday 3 December 
 Procession of floats not published 2 Dec: 12:00 pm to 4:30 pm and 6:00 pm to 8:00 pm; 3 Dec: 9:00 am to 12:00 pm, then from 6:00 pm 
 Fireworks not published 2 Dec: 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm; 3 Dec: from 7:30 pm 
 Danzaka climb not detailed in the 13 October notice evening of 3 December, time not published 
 Source: City of Chichibu, notice of 13 October 2026 , and for the 2025 reference times, Seibu Railway and Walkerplus , checked on 2 November 2026. 
 5. Getting from Tokyo: the Laview, special trains and fares
 The Laview from Ikebukuro, the simplest option
 The Laview « CHICHIBU » runs from Ikebukuro to Seibu-Chichibu in about 77 minutes. The adult fare checked in July 2026 by Ekitan is 1,700 yen. All seats are reserved, and the train runs more than ten return trips a day, according to the same source.
 From Seibu-Chichibu, the town centre is about 15 minutes on foot. Chichibu station, served by the Chichibu Railway, is about 5 minutes on foot from the centre, according to the guides we consulted.
 3 December: extra trains
 Seibu Railway announces extra limited express trains from Ikebukuro on 3 December 2026, starting from the 11:00 am slot and running about every 30 minutes. For this service, the limit is 8 tickets per person. Sales open on 3 November 2026, a public holiday in Japan.
 On 2 December, Seibu also changes one train to Seibu-Chichibu so that it starts at Seibu-Chichibu, with a special timetable between Hanno and Seibu-Chichibu. Check the exact timetable on Seibu’s website before you book, because the announcement does not give a full table.
 The JR Pass is not enough
 The Japan Rail Pass does not cover the Seibu lines, which are private railways. A route combining JR via Kumagaya and then the Chichibu Railway is described by a travel site, but its fare has not been confirmed on any official JR or Chichibu Railway page. Don’t count it in your budget without checking first.
 Getting from Tokyo to Chichibu: options and fares checked in 2026 Option Adult fare Journey time Booking 
 Laview from Ikebukuro 1,700 yen (checked July 2026) about 77 min reserved seats, more than 10 return trips a day 
 Ordinary train with a change at Hanno not checked against an official site about 2 h according to guides not stated 
 Special 3 December train (Seibu) not stated in the announcement from Ikebukuro, departures about every 30 min from 11:00 am 8 tickets per person at most, sales from 3 November 2026 
 Source: Ekitan, Laview CHICHIBU (July 2026 information) and Seibu Railway statement of 28 October 2026, checked on 2 November 2026. 
 6. Tickets, seats and 2026 offers
 Entry, seats and buses
 Guides describe the processions as free to watch. The city has not confirmed this explicitly in the notice we checked. Seated viewing places on the stalls, called 屋台観覧席, are paid: a 2025 guide gives 3,000 yen. We have not found them on sale for 2026.
 The city announces a THE ALFEE bus for 2026, leaving on 3 December, at 29,800 yen. According to the announcement of 26 October 2026, the offer includes seats for the fireworks. It is a separate product tied to a concert, not a requirement to see the festival.
 A 1,000 yen commemorative ticket is on sale from 1 December 2026 to 11 January 2027, according to the city. It is also tied to the music event and does not give access to the festival.
 Seats and offers linked to the Chichibu Night Festival, 2025 and 2026 Offer Price Date What to know 
 Stall viewing seat 屋台観覧席 3,000 yen 2025 (2026 sales not found) figure from a guide, to be confirmed 
 THE ALFEE bus 29,800 yen departs 3 December 2026 includes seats for the fireworks 
 Commemorative ticket 1,000 yen 1 December 2026 to 11 January 2027 tied to a concert, not the festival 
 Japan departure tax 3,000 yen since 1 July 2026 adds to your trip budget, not to the festival 
 Source: City of Chichibu, announcement of 26 October 2026 , JNTO, japan.travel (11 May 2026) and a 2025 guide, checked on 2 November 2026. 
 7. Fireworks, crowds and the Danzaka slope
 The fireworks: 2025 reference points
 According to 2025 sources, the fireworks are launched from Hitsujiyama Park (羊山公園). On 2 December 2025, the launch started around 7:00 pm and lasted about an hour. On 3 December, it began around 7:30 pm. Durations and shell counts vary between sources, so we quote neither a shell count nor a duration for 3 December.
 To watch the fireworks, Seibu recommended the car park of Chichibu City Hall and the area around Seibu-Chichibu station in 2025. These are 2025 reference points: the 2026 programme is not published.
 Crowds: 3 December is the busiest
 2 December is described as calmer, a lively evening. 3 December draws the biggest crowds, especially from 5:00 pm according to guides, around the Danzaka slope and the fireworks spots.
 For 3 December, the city notice announces traffic restrictions, but the map and temporary parking have not been published. Several sources recommend park-and-ride: parking on the outskirts and taking the train in. We advise against driving that day, and point you to the city’s map once it is out.
 Trains are packed once the festival ends: leave a buffer around the Laview or the special train you choose.
 8. Budget, accommodation, weather and entry formalities
 Indicative budget
 A guide estimates 8,000 to 12,000 yen for a full day in Chichibu, return trip and meals included, for a budget traveller. It is a guide’s estimate, not an official figure.
 Leaving Japan has also got more expensive recently. The departure tax rose from 1,000 to 3,000 yen on 1 July 2026, according to the JNTO . It adds to the cost of your trip, not to the price of the festival: about €16 for 3,000 yen at the June 2026 rate (to be updated).
 Accommodation: book early
 Accommodation in Chichibu is limited, according to the guides we consulted, who advise booking several months ahead. We found no official data on availability for the nights of 2 and 3 December 2026. If you cannot find a room in Chichibu, a stay in a nearby town means planning the trip back after the festival.
 Weather: expect cold
 Climate normals for 1991 to 2020 give an average December temperature of 4.0 °C in Chichibu, with an average high of 11.2 °C and an average low of -1.6 °C, according to time-j.net. Rainfall figures differ a lot between sites, so we do not quote them. We found no official rule for cancelling the festival in bad weather.
 Entry formalities
 This article does not set out the entry rules for UK passport holders. Check the entry requirements section of the FCDO’s Japan travel advice before you book.
 9. Usage rules and tips from the ground
 Drones and filming
 Seibu Railway’s festival page bans drones and filming. That page reflects the 2025 edition, and no 2026 rule has been published. The text does not say whether handheld video is covered, so treat it as covered and follow the staff on site.
 Tripods and photos
 We found no official rule on tripods. Check on the spot, because many Japanese religious sites restrict them. Never block a passage to take a photo.
 Follow the staff
 Spectators follow the instructions of the float crews and the police. On a busy route, they decide which areas stay open. A closed route is not up for debate: take another path, even if the view looks better somewhere else.
 10. Depending on your travel style
 First trip to Japan
 The Chichibu Night Festival suits a first trip to Japan well: one destination, a direct train and a festival that is easy to follow. Spend 2 December getting a feel for the town, then 3 December for the processions. If you are also passing through Tokyo, see our guide to Autumn Foliage in Tokyo 2026: Dates and Illuminations . If you are staying on into the New Year, see also Japan New Year 2027: What Closes and What to Do .
 Tight budget
 The Laview costs 1,700 yen. Guides present the ordinary train with a change at Hanno as cheaper but slower (about two hours), with no verified official fare.
 Couple or friends
 For two people, compare the cost of a day on site (a guide’s estimate: 8,000 to 12,000 yen per person, not official) with the cost of the return trip. On 3 December, the crowd slows every journey. One guide argues against arriving early for the peak of the night, since the Danzaka slope is closed to the public. That is an opinion, and we have not checked it.
 Families and reduced mobility
 3 December concentrates the crowd in the centre. We found no official accessibility information for wheelchair users or pushchairs in the sources we checked. Ask the city before you go.
 What other guides don’t tell you
 Four points are missing from the guides we checked, or appear in them without a date. Each one links to an official source, checked on 2 November 2026.
 The departure tax has been 3,000 yen since 1 July 2026. Several guides still quote 1,000 yen. The JNTO announced the rise in a publication of 11 May 2026 ( japan.travel , checked on 2 November 2026).
 The 3 December special trains have a limit. Seibu announces limited express trains from 11:00 am, about every 30 minutes, with 8 tickets per person at most, on sale from 3 November 2026 ( Seibu Railway statement , 28 October 2026, checked on 2 November 2026).
 The heritage status is more precise than guides suggest. National designation on 3 February 1979, and UNESCO listing in 2016 for the festivals of floats, hoko and yatai. Guides often just say « UNESCO heritage » ( Agency for Cultural Affairs record 203403 , checked on 2 November 2026).
 The 2026 timetables are not published. The city points to a future update for the processions, the fireworks and the traffic. Some guide pages still show 2026 times that repeat the 2025 ones ( City of Chichibu notice , 13 October 2026, checked on 2 November 2026).
 Frequently asked questions
 When is the Chichibu Night Festival in 2026? On 2 and 3 December 2026. Wednesday 2 December is the eve, called yoimiya, and Thursday 3 December is the main festival. The dates are confirmed by the City of Chichibu in its notice of 13 October 2026, and by Seibu Railway in its statement of 28 October 2026. The timetables for the processions and the fireworks are not published yet.
 Where is the Chichibu Night Festival held? In Chichibu, in Saitama Prefecture, around Chichibu Shrine. The town is about 77 minutes by Laview from Ikebukuro. From Seibu-Chichibu station, allow about 15 minutes on foot to the centre, or about 5 minutes from Chichibu station, served by the Chichibu Railway.
 Is the Chichibu Night Festival free? Guides describe the processions as free to watch, but the city has not confirmed it explicitly in the notice we checked. Seated viewing places on the stalls, called 屋台観覧席, are paid: one guide gives 3,000 yen for 2025. The THE ALFEE bus, announced for 3 December 2026 at 29,800 yen, is a separate offer.
 How do you get from Tokyo to Chichibu? The simplest option is the Laview from Ikebukuro: about 77 minutes, 1,700 yen for an adult, reserved seats, according to Ekitan (July 2026). The Japan Rail Pass does not cover the Seibu lines. On 3 December, Seibu adds limited express trains from 11:00 am, with a maximum of 8 tickets per person.
 Is there a difference between 2025 and 2026? The dates follow the same pattern, 2 and 3 December. But the city has not yet published the 2026 timetables for the processions, the fireworks or the traffic. The 2025 times are a reference, not a programme. The 2026 special trains, for their part, are announced by Seibu Railway.
 When and where can you see the fireworks? In 2025, the launch started around 7:00 pm on 2 December and around 7:30 pm on 3 December, from Hitsujiyama Park. Seibu then recommended the car park of Chichibu City Hall or the area around Seibu-Chichibu station. The 2026 programme is not out yet, so wait for the city’s notice.
 Should you book accommodation? Yes, if you want to sleep in Chichibu on 2 and 3 December. Rooms are limited, and guides advise booking several months ahead. We found no official data on availability for those nights. If you cannot find anything, plan the trip back after the festival.
 Can you film or fly a drone? Drones and filming are banned according to the Seibu Railway page on the festival, in its 2025 version. No 2026 rule has been published. The text does not say whether handheld video is covered, so assume it is, and follow the staff on site.
 Sources
 City of Chichibu, notice « 令和8年「秩父夜祭」について »  : dates, upcoming timetables, updated 13 October 2026
 City of Chichibu, THE ALFEE bus announcement  : departure on 3 December 2026, 29,800 yen (26 October 2026)
 City of Chichibu, festival page  : six floats (checked on 2 November 2026)
 Seibu Railway, statement of 28 October 2026  : special trains, 8-ticket limit, sales from 3 November 2026
 Seibu Railway, festival page  : 2025 data, drones and filming
 Agency for Cultural Affairs, record 203403  : designation of 3 February 1979, UNESCO mention of 2016
 JNTO, japan.travel  : departure tax of 3,000 yen (11 May 2026)
 Ekitan, Laview CHICHIBU  : journey time, fare and seats (July 2026 information)
 Walkerplus, Chichibu fireworks  : 2025 times
 FCDO, Japan travel advice: entry requirements (gov.uk)  : entry rules for UK passport holders
 time-j.net  : 1991-2020 climate normals for Chichibu
 Sources consulted on 2 November 2026. The 2026 timetables will be added as soon as the city publishes them.
